A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNRI research work. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original image reconstruction, editing, interpolation, rare-concept generation, and human-evaluation results, together with appendix ablations and failure analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds computational measurements, a low-likelihood COCO comparison, and additional qualitative editing experiments.

M1.justification: The residual objective, Gaussian guidance term, scalar Newton-Raphson update, initialization, and scheduler formulations remain unchanged. The expanded guidance explanation and corrected equation references do not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: The underlying COCO, PIE-Bench, and ImageNet-based coverage remains. v5 adds a deliberately non-typical COCO test population in Appendix I and simultaneous editing of different object categories in Appendix K, extending test scenarios within the existing image-editing domain.

E2.justification: EditFriendly, already present in v4's editing comparisons, is added to PIE-Bench Table 1 and the reconstruction comparison in Table H2. Appendix I adds a dedicated Anderson-acceleration comparison beyond v4's existing AIDI evaluations. The broader comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The original benchmark and human-study protocols remain unchanged. Added evaluations use Flux.1 for qualitative PIE-Bench comparisons, select 300 COCO images with the lowest reported likelihood, introduce NFE measurements, and compare memory and timing on A100 and RTX 3090Ti GPUs.

E4.justification: v5 retains the guidance ablation, lambda sensitivity, contraction measurements, and caption-mismatch failure analysis. It substantially broadens supplementary analysis through the low-likelihood Anderson comparison, NFE and hardware-memory studies, and simultaneous multi-object editing case studies in Appendices H–K.

E5.justification: The existing averaged results and plot error bars are retained. v5 introduces no new repeated-run counts, experimental seed protocols, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 rows and Tables 2–3 retain their values, but Tables H1–J1 substantially expand reported findings. Examples include GNRI's 6 NFEs; EditFriendly's 26.1 versus GNRI's 23.9 reconstruction PSNR, with inversion times of 32.3 versus 0.521 seconds; and low-likelihood PSNR of 25.8 versus Anderson's 18.3. New qualitative results appear in Figures F2 and K1. Figure 4 also newly claims a 2× speedup over DDIM, which conflicts with its retained runtime plot.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Appendix A derivation, and contraction argument remain unchanged, with the latter moving from Appendix B to C. New Appendix B expands the existing discussion of objectives without zero crossings but supplies no new proof, derivation, or formal convergence result.

C1.justification: The central claims remain efficient, training-free guided inversion, rapid editing, and improved interpolation and rare-concept generation. Explicitly mentioning flow-matching compatibility clarifies coverage already represented by Flux.1 in v4 rather than introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B explicitly connects the existing non-zero-minimum discussion to GNRI's nonnegative objective. Appendices H and I explain the stochastic-inversion fidelity/speed tradeoff and distinguish distribution-aware guidance from Anderson acceleration, including possible application of guidance to other iterative methods.

D1.justification: Appendix H explains the reported 6 NFEs as four steps averaging 1.5 Newton-Raphson iterations. Appendix J specifies the 40 GB A100 and 24 GB RTX 3090Ti hardware. These extend technical disclosure; the original implementation information and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 newly credits Hong and Garibi for applying norms to inversion residuals, clarifying GNRI's distinction. Appendix I adds substantive positioning against Anderson acceleration. Reference deduplication and author/year corrections concern existing works rather than newly added research.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains intact, with localized explanatory edits and corrected implicit-equation references. The appendices are split and reorganized, including a separate no-zero-crossing discussion. v5 also adds acknowledgments, changes the conference header, and condenses affiliations.

P2.justification: Tables H1, H2, I1, and J1 and Figures F2 and K1 substantially expand the visual presentation of computational comparisons, difficult inputs, and editing examples. Table 1 gains a comparator row; Figure 1 replaces the notebook's Work edit with ICLR; Figures 3–4 receive label and caption edits. Existing appendix figures are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added NFE, memory, EditFriendly, and low-likelihood comparisons make computational costs, robustness, and reconstruction tradeoffs more assessable than in v4. These are useful, focused additions to an already extensive evaluation. The new Figure 4 claim of a 2× speedup over DDIM contradicts its plot, introducing a limited accuracy defect that reduces, but does not outweigh, those benefits.
